translations.title: Retirement planning in your 30s: the decade that does the heavy lifting
translations.excerpt: Money invested at 30 has thirty years to compound. The same rupee invested at 45 has fifteen. That gap is the whole argument.

blocks.text: At 30, retirement feels like someone else's problem. It is, in a sense: the person you will be at 60 depends on what you do now, and they cannot vote. Here is the case for starting this year.

A ₹10,000 monthly SIP at {return_equity} a year grows to about ₹3.5 crore over 30 years. Start five years later and it reaches roughly ₹1.9 crore. The five missed years cost more than every rupee you would have invested in them.

Take today's monthly expenses, inflate them at {inflation_default} to your retirement age, and plan for a corpus that can pay that amount, rising with inflation, until about 85. The retirement corpus calculator does the maths and tells you the SIP that closes the gap.

items: Max the employer EPF match; it is the only guaranteed 100% return you will see.
Add NPS if your employer offers it, for the extra {nps_80ccd1b_limit} deduction under 80CCD(1B) in the old regime.
Then equity index funds through SIPs, stepped up with every salary hike.

blocks.text: Equity-heavy in your 30s is appropriate because you have three decades to ride out downturns. The mix moves toward debt as retirement approaches.

items: Start now; the first decade compounds longest.
Target a corpus, not a round number.
EPF match first, then NPS, then equity SIPs with annual step-ups.
